details: New York Federal Reserve President John Williams expressed optimism that inflationary pressures will gradually ease. However, he affirmed the U.S. central bank's readiness to implement further rate hikes if inflation deviates from its target path. This stance follows the Federal Open Market Committee's recent decision to keep interest rates unchanged, despite some dissenting votes favoring a hike due to persistent inflation above the 2% target. Financial markets are closely watching core inflation data for future policy direction.
title: Fed's Williams: Inflation to Ease, Rate Hikes Possible if Not

details: Eurozone government bond yields decreased as oil prices fell more than 5% due to hopes of easing tensions in the Middle East. This reduction in geopolitical risk premium has improved investor sentiment, leading markets to temper expectations for additional European Central Bank (ECB) interest rate increases. Lower energy prices are generally viewed as easing inflationary pressures, potentially giving central banks more flexibility.
title: Oil Price Decline Eases Inflation Fears, Lowers Eurozone Yields

details: U.S. economic growth decelerated to an annualized rate of 1.5% in the second quarter of 2026. Despite this slowdown in the headline figure, consumer spending showed resilience, rising by 3.2%. The bond market displayed conflicting signals, with the Wall Street Journal suggesting rising long-term Treasury yields might reflect expectations of stronger economic growth, while the New York Times interpreted it as doubts about the Federal Reserve's commitment to tackling inflation.
sourceName: Wall Street Journal (via WNG.org and Business Finance News)
title: US Q2 GDP Slows to 1.5%; Treasury Yields Show Mixed Signals

details: Switzerland's annual inflation rate eased to 0.4% in July, a slight decrease from 0.5% in June and in line with analysts' expectations. The moderation was primarily driven by a decline in petroleum product prices. This continued low inflationary pressure in Switzerland provides the Swiss National Bank (SNB) with room to maintain its benchmark rate at 0%, as inflation remains within its 0-2% target range.
title: Swiss Annual Inflation Dips to 0.4% in July, Below Forecasts
